name: Shay Lloyd
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “My first foster dog ate the receipt for our secondhand sofa.” On Wednesday, near Juniper Street, Shay knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I fostered both litters. Their ears fold the same way until somebody says dinner.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a small enamel bird on the lapel. Shay has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with short black hair swept back. Shay gives a little nod before asking a hard question during a conversation.
personality: Shay is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To give both families a trustworthy way to tell the dogs apart.
family: Kit Salcedo is Shay’s younger cousin. A parent had a second job that nobody mentioned at school. Years later the family discovered two sets of friends who thought they knew entirely different people. Shay is slow to assume that a job title explains anybody. Asked about *The blue suit*, Kit says, “I gave the borrowed shoes a polish on the bank steps.”
connections: Eden Sun (dog guardian). The fosterer helps the new guardian distinguish two members of one litter.
